findings.title: Missing review directory breaks `stats reviews --json`
findings.description: `stats_reviews` returns the human message at `src/squadron/cli/commands/stats.py:61-63` before checking `as_json` at `src/squadron/cli/commands/stats.py:64-65`. In a project without `project-documents/user/reviews`, `sq stats reviews --json` prints `No review directory at ...`, which is not JSON, despite the option help and the `reviews_report_json` serializer in `src/squadron/cli/stats_views.py#reviews_report_json`. `tests/cli/test_stats.py#test_reviews_missing_dir_exits_0_with_message` only covers the non-JSON path, so this machine-facing contract is untested.

findings.title: Review report counts any frontmatter-bearing markdown as a review
findings.description: The loop at `src/squadron/stats/reviews_report.py:67-80` accepts every top-level `*.md` with parseable YAML frontmatter; it only filters on slice, `runId`, and unreadable frontmatter. It does not check `docType: review`, `reviewType`, or a review filename pattern. `src/squadron/review/resolution_artifact.py:179-183` writes resolution artifacts into the same `REVIEWS_DIR`, so a sibling frontmatter document can become a bogus review row with an empty `UsageRecord`, inflating the denominator in the totals. Add a review-artifact predicate and a test with a real non-review sibling document.

findings.title: SDK compact failures discard provider telemetry
findings.description: `SDKExecutionSession.dispatch` attaches completed telemetry to `ProviderError` in `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py#dispatch`, but `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/compact.py:78-91` catches every exception and returns a failure `ActionResult` with no `metadata`; only the success path at `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/compact.py:93-96` stamps usage. A failed compact that spent tokens therefore has no usage row in `sq stats run`, contradicting the slice’s “failed actions record what they spent” requirement. The new tests in `tests/pipeline/actions/test_compact.py#Usage records` cover success, no-spend, and missing capture, but not this failure mode.

findings.title: `stats reviews` cannot identify subscription aliases from real review artifacts
findings.description: `src/squadron/stats/reviews_report.py#_record` reconstructs `UsageRecord.alias` from frontmatter `requestedModel` only when that value is itself a known alias. In production, `src/squadron/review/review_client.py#run_review_with_profile` sets `result.requested_model` to the resolved model id, and `src/squadron/review/persistence.py#format_review_markdown` writes `requestedModel` only when `model_substituted` is true. The alias passed to `run_review_with_profile` is used for cost resolution but never persisted. As a result, `src/squadron/cli/stats_views.py#cost_cell` usually sees `alias=None` and prints subscription provider costs as `$... prov` instead of `$... api-rate equiv.`. `tests/stats/test_reviews_report.py#test_requested_model_maps_to_alias_only_when_known` uses synthetic `requestedModel: opus` frontmatter rather than the real artifact shape.

findings.title: `stats run` accepts path-shaped run IDs
findings.description: The CLI passes the raw `run_id` argument to `run_usage_report` at `src/squadron/cli/commands/stats.py:34-41`. `src/squadron/pipeline/state.py#state_file_name` simply returns `f"{run_id}.json"` with no validation, and `src/squadron/pipeline/state.py#StateManager._state_path` joins that name to `runs_dir`. Absolute paths and `..` segments can therefore escape the configured state directory and read arbitrary readable `.json` files; malformed files also leak the resolved path in the error message. Validate `run_id` at the CLI boundary by rejecting separators/absolute paths or by resolving and confirming the parent is `runs_dir`, then add regression tests for absolute and traversal-shaped IDs.

structured_findings.summary: Review report counts any frontmatter-bearing markdown as a review
SDK compact failures discard provider telemetry
`stats reviews` cannot identify subscription aliases from real review artifacts
